text:
incident-bot: PAGER — inference.service.high_error_rate detected in us-west-2b (region: us-west-2). Current symptom: burst of 5xx + stream timeouts from inference frontends. Automations: created incident INC-2026-1057, alerted #incidents and on-call. Link: https://redwood.ops/inc/INC-2026-1057

mike_oncall: acked. I'm looking at SLO dashboard — 95p latency spiked ~1200ms, error rate ~7% for last 8m. Creating short triage.

anya_eng: adding traces — seeing a lot of grpc connection resets from the runtime layer to workers in us-west-2b. KV cache miss rate jumped too.

leo_netops: I'm seeing network retransmits at the AZ egress. Route table shows several ENI retransmit bursts around 12:07:20 UTC. Could be host-level NIC queuing.

mike_oncall: good. Devex, can we divert traffic to other AZs quickly? We want minimal customer impact.

devops-bot: autoscale action suggested: bring up 3 nodes in us-west-2c (fallback pool) with model-serve-profile=low-latency-1. Command queued: `rctl cluster create --zone us-west-2c --type g5 --count 3 --tag inference-fallback`

jules: I'll take network lead. Mike handing off to me if this needs cross-AZ steering. mike_oncall: handing off, I have to join a customer call in 5. Jules, I put all logs in the incident runbook. :thumbsup:

mike_oncall: note for CS — customers with pinned dedicated capacity in us-west-2b may see errors if they were pinned to affected hosts. Olivia, please gather a short list of top affected accounts by error-rate.

olivia_cs: on it. Pulling from the customer-impact dashboard now. Early list: acct-984, acct-1312, acct-4427 (high 5xx), a few smaller dev orgs with ephemeral dedicated slots. Will post ETA for outreach in 10m.

anya_eng: quick check command to confirm worker health:
```
# curl health on worker
curl -sS http://10.2.45.17:8080/healthz
# sample output
{"status":"degraded","kvcache_miss":0.37,"cpu_load":0.92}
```

leo_netops: AWS console shows increased 'NetworkPacketsIn' and 'NetworkPacketsOut' errors on g5 instances in us-west-2b. Also seeing elevated 'InstanceNetworkInterface' RxErrors. Filing a support ticket with AWS (case 1234567890).

devops-bot: autoscale started in us-west-2c: instance ids i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h,i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a,i-0123456789abcdef0. Healthchecks running.

jules: I'm going to shift a fraction of traffic away from us-west-2b using the router weight delta to 20% for 2m then 10% until stable. Applying now: `routerctl set-weight inference--usw2b 0.2` -> success.

mike_oncall: reaction :white_check_mark: Nice. Any signs of recovery in host networking?

leo_netops: slight improvement post-weight-shift; retransmits down ~40% in the last 3m but still above baseline. AWS support says they're investigating a host NIC firmware issue affecting some hypervisors. They recommend migrating instances off affected hosts.

anya_eng: runtime telemetry shows K/V cache warmup in new us-west-2c nodes; p95 latency on routed traffic to usw2c about 180ms now. Error rate for those requests ~0.4%. Good fallback.

olivia_cs: posting customer note draft for affected accounts: "We observed degraded inference performance and transient errors in us-west-2b — we have shifted traffic to other AZs and are provisioning fallback capacity. We're actively monitoring; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Approve?

jules: approve. Send.

mike_oncall: plan for next 30m: 1) Keep traffic shifted to 10-20% to us-west-2b only. 2) Migrate remaining pinned instances off affected hosts where possible. 3) Let autoscaled fallback in 2c handle steady load. 4) If AWS completes host migration, we can shift back gradually.

devops-bot: migration suggestion: `rctl migrate --instances i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h --destination-pool us-west-2d-pool-2` (dry-run approved).

leo_netops: starting host-level instance evacuations for flagged hosts. I'll post progress.

jules: handing to leo for net ops execution. I'm going to update the incident header and prepare postmortem skeleton. @mike_oncall take the final oncall summary when you're back.

mike_oncall: thanks. I'll rejoin in 20. Good handoff.

devops-bot: Migration dry-run completed, planned migration steps queued. Estimated time per instance ~3m.

leo_netops: first host migration finished, instances reattached to healthy hypervisor. Error spikes dropped for that batch. Continuing.

olivia_cs: customers acct-1312 and acct-4427 acknowledged receipt and paused heavy jobs while we stabilize. acct-984 asked for ETA, I gave 45m conservative.

jules: routing weights now: us-west-2b 0.1, us-west-2c 0.6, us-west-2d 0.3. Will keep 10% to b for validation.

mike_oncall: good. Moving to monitoring mode. If error rate drops below 0.5% for 15m we de-escalate.

incident-bot: Note: on-call handoff scheduled at 3976503000 (UTC). Next responder: sam_oncall.

jules: quick post-mortem notes for now: root cause suspected host NIC firmware bug triggered by increased egress bursts; AWS investigating and doing hypervisor remediation. Short-term mitigations: cross-AZ traffic steering, instance evacuations, autoscale fallback pools. Follow-ups: validate pinned-capacity behaviors, add health-based routing to avoid single-host clustering.

olivia_cs: I'll maintain customer comms channel and set targeted messages once we have final timeline.

mike_oncall: closing loop for my handoff — I will post a 1-paragraph summary for ops channels once we hit the 15m threshold. Great job team. :clap:

jules: marking incident as "mitigated" in INC-2026-1057; we'll keep it open for RCA until AWS confirms host remediation.

devops-bot: autoscale monitors: fallback pool steady; kvcache hit rate improving.

leo_netops: last update before I step out: AWS support now confirmed hypervisor-side NIC firmware push queued for the rack; ETA unknown. We'll avoid pushing non-essential workloads into us-west-2b until confirmed.

mike_oncall: copy. Ending active coordination. Will update timeline and final RCA notes later.

incident-bot: INC-2026-1057 status updated -> mitigated.
